poster_title: ESSAYBENCH: Evaluating Large Language Models in Multi-Genre Chinese Essay Writing
authors: Fan Gao, Dongyuan Li, Ding Xia, Fei Mi, Yasheng Wang, Lifeng Shang, Baojun Wang

content: Chinese essay writing is crucial in educational contexts.
LLMs' capabilities in this domain are underexplored.
Existing benchmarks lack fine-grained metrics.
Need for a more comprehensive evaluation framework.
Aims to capture structural and rhetorical complexities.
Current evaluation methods are too coarse-grained.
Neglect unique characteristics of Chinese essays.
Difficulty in revealing specific weaknesses.
Need for genre-specific criteria.
Propose ESSAYBENCH with 728 real-world prompts.
panels.figure_caption: Overview of the ESSAYBENCH dataset curation, representative prompts, and the evaluation framework.

content: Develop a fine-grained, genre-specific scoring framework.
Introduce a dependency-weighted score aggregation strategy.
Human agreement study and quality sensitivity analysis.
Framework aligns closely with human judgments.
panels.figure_caption: Comparison between coarse-grained evaluation methods and our fine-grained and genre-oriented framework for ESSAYBENCH.

content: Benchmark 15 large-scale LLMs on Chinese essay writing.
panels.figure_caption: Dataset Statistics. Note that Open denotes Open-Ended sets, Cons. refers to Constrained sets.

content: Framework significantly improves the ability to distinguish essay quality.
Detailed comparisons of LLMs' capabilities across different genres.
panels.figure_caption: Comparison of LLMs Performance across different genres.

content: ESSAYBENCH addresses the gap in fine-grained and genre-specific evaluation.
Benchmark and evaluation protocol can advance LLM use in educational settings.
Inspires future research on essay generation.
